subject: astronomy

moments.title: Herschel maps the Milky Way
moments.body: Herschel's 'On the Construction of the Heavens' uses star counts to argue the Milky Way is a disc-shaped system. Caroline Herschel, his sister and collaborator, discovers eight comets and catalogues nebulae. William also discovers Uranus (1781), infrared radiation (1800) and over 2,500 nebulae.
moments.takeaway: The first attempt to map our galaxy's shape was made by a brother-sister team in 18th-century England. Caroline was the first woman paid as an astronomer.

moments.title: The Great Debate: Curtis vs Shapley
moments.who: Heber Curtis (Lick) and Harlow Shapley (Mount Wilson)
moments.body: At the Smithsonian on 26 April 1920, Curtis and Shapley debate whether spiral nebulae are inside the Milky Way (Shapley) or separate galaxies (Curtis). Each is half-right: Shapley correctly enlarges the Milky Way; Curtis correctly identifies spiral nebulae as external galaxies. The debate is settled by Hubble in 1924.
moments.takeaway: The size of the universe was openly debated by professional astronomers within living memory. We did not know we were in a galaxy among galaxies a century ago.

moments.title: Hubble resolves Andromeda
moments.body: Using the 100-inch Hooker telescope on Mount Wilson and Leavitt's Cepheid period-luminosity relation, Hubble measures the distance to the Andromeda 'nebula' (M31): ~900,000 light years (modern: 2.5 million). It is far outside the Milky Way. The universe contains other galaxies.
moments.takeaway: On a single photographic plate Hubble's note 'VAR!' next to a Cepheid in Andromeda effectively settled the question. The plate is preserved at Carnegie Observatories.

now.title: Galaxies today
now.body: Observable universe: ~2 trillion galaxies (JWST has revised this estimate upward). The Milky Way is one spiral galaxy in the Local Group, which is part of the Virgo Supercluster, which is part of Laniakea. We are still mapping the local structure.
now.open_questions: How did the first galaxies form? JWST is observing galaxies at z>10 (less than 500 million years after the Big Bang) that are larger and more mature than models predicted.

reflection: Caroline Herschel received a salary of £50/year from George III in 1787 — the first woman paid as a professional astronomer. She lived to 97 (died 1848) and received the Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society in 1828.
